page: Amazon Web Services r8i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 virtual CPUs and 16 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing the Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong capabilities in specific processing tasks. The instance achieves top-25% performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, Passmark CPU scores, and single-threaded gzip compression. It also demonstrates strong performance in image and text processing, as well as static web serving throughput. However, its stress-ng CPU performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall within the average range. For machine learning workloads, the hardware-assisted Advanced Matrix Extensions contribute to top-10% text generation speeds for small 135M parameter LLM models, though performance drops to the bottom 25% when executing text generation on large 70B parameter models due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8i.8xlarge offers high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX allows the instance to handle specialized vector and matrix operations efficiently without the added cost of GPU hardware. This profile is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, medium-scale language model inference, and software compilation tasks.
